Michelle: Heads-up — noticed a weird pattern on canary where memory climbs over long-context sessions even though eviction_counter is ticking. Eviction rate looks normal but residency % reported by sampler is dropping. Can anyone help correlate signals before I dig deeper?

Raj: Do you have a short excerpt of metrics + a timeline? e.g. residencies, evictions, heap RSS, and any KV page churn counters?

Michelle: Yep pasted a minimal extract below. Timeline is ~30m during extended chat session.

Michelle: ```
time=00:00 residency=0.78 eviction_count=120 kv_pages_free=2400 kv_pages_used=7200 rss_mb=520
time=00:10 residency=0.66 eviction_count=180 kv_pages_free=2350 kv_pages_used=7250 rss_mb=560
time=00:20 residency=0.55 eviction_count=230 kv_pages_free=2200 kv_pages_used=7400 rss_mb=625
time=00:30 residency=0.42 eviction_count=300 kv_pages_free=2000 kv_pages_used=7600 rss_mb=710
```

Michelle: Observations: eviction_count increments steadily (not a single big spike), residency falls, used pages increases, RSS grows even after evictions.

Oliver: That screams fragmentation or small-page churn — evictions might be removing non-contiguous fragments so allocator can't reclaim large contiguous ranges. Do we have a per-page-size free bucket metric?

Dina: Also check KV reuse rate (how often the same key/frame is accessed) vs new page allocations. If reuse drops, cache churn will look like growth even with evictions.

Kevin: For dashboards: I'd plot three lines on same X axis: residency %, eviction rate (per-min), and delta(RSS) per minute. Add a stacked area of kv_pages_used by size-class if available. Correlate with request QPS and average sequence length.

Raj: Another quick idea: correlate the sampler residency vs a full scan residency (a heavier but accurate probe). Sampler can undercount when hotset shifts to large objects. If sampler=0.42 but full_scan=0.6, that's sampling bias.

Michelle: Good point re sampler bias — we do have periodic full scans but they're 5x more expensive. I'll pull the last full-scan.

sre-bot: Incident note created: #INC-2026-kv-page-churn — triggered at 2134567920 for rising RSS on canary cluster.

Oliver: Quick triage checklist: 1) attach request traces for a long session 2) pull allocator fragmentation histogram 3) export per-size free buckets 4) run a short full-scan residency and compare.

Dina: If we confirm fragmentation, mitigation options: compacting GC-like pass (expensive), larger page coalescing in allocator, or a temporary pinning policy that prefers eviction of small fragments. Each has perf tradeoffs.

Michelle: I'm going to add a temporary dashboard tile for sampler vs full-scan residency + eviction rate and annotate the time ranges. Can someone suggest alert thresholds?

Kevin: Alert idea: when residency drops >20% within 15m AND rss increases >100MB in same window => page-churn-warning. Set to P3 initially.

Raj: For root cause, also check kernel selection variants — we recently flipped to the new fused-kernel path on canary. If it changes access patterns (batching behavior) it could increase KV tail accesses and reduce temporal locality.

Michelle: Ah — good catch. We did roll fused-kernel last night on that pool. I'll repro on a fixed kernel build and compare.

Oliver: If you need a quick profiler command: `./kv-prof --hist --by-size --since 2134566000` gives per-size hotness histogram that helped us last time.

Michelle: Thanks all — I'll post the baseline after the full-scan and the kernel A/B. If anyone wants to co-investigate ping me. :pray: 

Kevin: Happy to help with dashboarding. If you include the metric names I'll add tiles and a short runbook blurb. :thumbsup:
